title: A soul shown both paths
translation: By the soul and the One who fashioned it, then inspired it with its wickedness and its mindfulness of God! Whoever purifies it has succeeded, and whoever buries it has failed.
body: Ibn Kathir gives **two readings of verse 9**: whoever purifies himself **by obedience** succeeds, or, via Ibn ʿAbbas, the one **whose soul God purifies**. In verse 8 God “explained good and evil” to it. Deuteronomy sets a like choice before Israel; the **Augsburg Confession (XVIII)** grants the will civil righteousness, not spiritual righteousness **without the Holy Spirit**.
question: In verse 9, who does the purifying: the person, or God? Which reading does the wording “man zakkāhā” favour?
source_label: Ibn Kathir on 91:7-10 · Augsburg Confession XVIII
reading: Angelika Neuwirth, Der Koran 1: Frühmekkanische Suren (2011)
